READING

**Checking the arithmetic first**

VELLACOTT: 3,050,000 – 610,000 + 240,000 = 2,680,000. Confirmed.
TARNSIDE: 1,420,000 + 310,000 = 1,730,000. Confirmed.
Capital premium of VELLACOTT over TARNSIDE: 950,000.

**What the fuel saving does to that premium**

At GBP 190,000 a year, the extra 950,000 is recovered in exactly five years. That is year-six breakeven at flat fuel prices — and fuel prices are unlikely to fall. From year six onward VELLACOTT is ahead by 190,000 a year in running costs alone, without counting any difference in maintenance trajectory between a 2017 hull and a 1995 hull.

**The hull age question is not cosmetic**

TARNSIDE fixes the one thing the surveyor identified. It does not fix the age of the vessel. In January 2028, when the re-engined Brindlemere comes back into service, she will be thirty-three years old. The hull passed in March 2026 with no steelwork required — that is good news — but a clean hull survey is a snapshot, not a guarantee of the next decade. Classification societies resurvey on a five-year cycle; the next hull survey falls around 2031, by which point the Brindlemere will be thirty-six. The Suilvenaig's first survey under your ownership falls around the same calendar year but on a nine-year-old hull. The risk profiles are materially different. TARNSIDE does not solve the medium-term vessel problem; it postpones it by roughly one planning cycle while consuming 1.73 million of capital.

**The Kittiwake window**

The 610,000 valuation holds until 2027-02-11. If VELLACOTT is chosen, the Suilvenaig handover is available from 2026-11-20, which means the Brindlemere can be sold before the valuation lapses with several weeks of margin. Timing is workable.

**Masters**

This is the sharpest operational risk in VELLACOTT. All nine masters need a six-week endorsement and two will retire rather than sit it. That takes the rota from nine to seven — before accounting for holiday, sickness and any retirements that were coming anyway. Seven masters covering eleven crossings a day across a May-to-September peak is tight, but it is not the same thing as impossible: operators on comparable routes run on shorter lists. The mitigation is to start recruitment now, treating the two departures as already-confirmed vacancies, and to stagger the endorsement course so that at no point is the rota uncovered. The endorsement requirement is a cost and a planning burden; it is not a reason to decline the better vessel.

**The insurance gap**

This is the one genuinely unresolved material fact. The broker has not quoted on the Suilvenaig. It is conceivable — though unlikely for a nine-year-old purpose-built ferry — that the premium uplift or a change in terms would materially alter the economics. This number must be obtained before contracts are exchanged, and VELLACOTT should be confirmed conditional on the insurance quote being within acceptable range. That said, the absence of a quote is not a reason to default to TARNSIDE; it is a reason to instruct the broker this week.

**Summary position**

TARNSIDE costs 1.73 million, keeps the status quo on masters and insurance, and leaves you with a 1995 hull that will need further capital attention before 2035. VELLACOTT costs 950,000 more in capital, recovers that premium within five years from fuel alone, gives you a 2017 hull with a plausible twenty-plus-year forward life, and eliminates the yard period and charter entirely. The staffing issue is real and requires active management. The insurance issue requires a quote before commitment. Neither outweighs the structural advantage of acquiring a younger vessel whose operating cost advantage pays for itself within a single parliamentary term.

---

READING
  The capital premium of VELLACOTT over TARNSIDE is GBP 950,000. The annual fuel saving is GBP 190,000, producing a five-year payback on that premium from fuel alone. TARNSIDE spends GBP 1.73M to keep a 1995 hull in service for a further planning cycle, at the end of which the vessel replacement question returns, larger and more urgent. VELLACOTT acquires a 2017 hull with a substantially longer serviceable life, eliminates the yard period and charter, and breaks even on the extra capital by 2032. The two master retirements and the outstanding insurance quote are genuine action items — the insurance quote in particular must be obtained before contracts are signed — but neither constitutes grounds to prefer an outcome that is financially and operationally weaker over a ten-to-fifteen-year horizon.

CALL
  VELLACOTT

GROUNDS
  The GBP 950,000 capital premium over TARNSIDE is recovered within five years of fuel savings alone, and TARNSIDE merely defers the vessel-replacement question onto a hull that will be thirty-six at its next classification survey.
